self-esteem and stress reactivity during social conflict - and not during negative social evaluation - partially mediates the relationship between social phobia and disordered eating in a nonclinical sample.
self-esteem and reactivity to social conflict partially mediated the relationship social anxiety and disorded eating.
social anxiety is linked to disordered eating through self-esteem and reactivity to stress, particularly during conflict.

the relationship between social and eating disorders.
the role that social anxiety plays in the development and maintenance of disordered eating.
the relationship between social factors and disordered eating behaviours.

the current study has demonstrated that self-esteem is a powerful mechanism that can maintain eating disorders in those with social anxiety.

self-esteem and interpersonal conflicts partially mediate the relationship that is found between social anxiety and eating disorder.

social anxiety is associated with disordered eating, and this is mediated by stress reactivity, and self esteem.
social anxiety and dis-ordered eating share common mechanisms that can help to understand and treat both of these disorders.
